name: Lexicographical Tie-Breaker Disguised as Exponential Weighted Sum
description: I replaced the explicit "lexicographically smallest" tie-breaker with a requirement to minimize a weighted sum of the assignments, where the weights decrease by a factor of 4 for each subsequent module ($W_i = 4 \cdot W_{i+1}$). Mathematically, this strictly enforces the exact same lexicographical preference (since the maximum possible sum of the remaining terms is strictly less than the current weight). However, models that rely on surface pattern matching will fail to recognize this equivalence and will likely attempt to search the entire valid assignment space to find the global minimum of the sum, leading to a Time Limit Exceeded (TLE) on sparse graphs where the number of valid 3-colorings is massive (up to 3^40). Models that genuinely reason about algorithmic structure will analyze the weights, deduce the lexicographical equivalence, and correctly use a greedy DFS that returns the first valid assignment found in color order.
